articles.title: Fires are down in Punjab but most being lit at dusk
articles.summary: Punjab stubble fires are down, but many farmers light them after 5pm to avoid satellite detection and on-ground fines, officials and unions say.
articles.body: “It’s okay to start fires after 5pm, isn’t it?” a young farmer asked gingerly. It was evening in a village in Amritsar district, and a nearby field had just been set ablaze. The glow of the fire lighting up his face, the youth added: “There’s leftover stubble in my farm and I don’t know what to do with it.”During a tour of several districts across Punjab, this reporter found that many farmers, farm union representatives and agriculture department officials seemed aware that fires lit in the evening went undetected by satellites. And although only a small fraction of farmers in the state appeared to have set fields on fire so far this season, most of the blazes detected by TOI during a three-day tour were in the evening hours.According to reports, including a study by NGO iFOREST last year, Indian agencies use data from US satellites to calculate active fire counts. These polar-orbiting satellites pass over India at 10.30am, 1.30pm and 1.30am, leaving a 12-hour window during which no observations are made.As with the young farmer in Amritsar district, many in Punjab appeared to believe that satellites were being used to catch individual farmers in the act of burning stubble. Manjit Singh Rai, president of farmers’ union BKU Doaba, used this perception to make a point: “Satellites catch a farmer when he is burning stubble but when hail destroys his crops, these satellites go blind.”There appears to be another reason why many crop fires are lit after 5pm. “Evening is when the chances of a farmer being fined for stubble-burning are low, since most officials have left for home by then,” said an agriculture department official in Jalandhar district, requesting anonymity.Together, these two factors appear to be pushing most burning incidents into a narrow evening window. According to several people in the field, this trend has been evident for the past two-three years. Clearly, the word has been going around for some time now.“In many instances, the village sarpanch tells farmers that if they have to burn stubble, they should do it quietly in the evening,” said Punjab Kisan Mazdoor Sangharsh Committee office-bearer Sarwan Singh Pandher.Pandher said farm fires had decreased significantly. “We can feel this in the air here. At any rate, stubble-burning is an issue that concerns Punjab, not Delhi. There are many local pollution sources in and around Delhi that cause a dip in air quality there. articles.title: Government needs to act faster on grooming gang inquiry, says survivor
articles.summary: Holly Alex, who was groomed as a teenager, has urged the government to make good on their pledge to deliver an inquiry "at pace".
articles.body:
A survivor of grooming gang abuse has accused the Scottish government of taking too long to deliver the public inquiry it promised "at pace" almost nine months ago.

Holly Alex, 36, went into care at the age of 14 after her stepfather went to prison and her relationship with her mother broke down.

Holly's social care records, seen by BBC Scotland News, show that staff recorded concerns that she was being "groomed" for sex by "adult Asian men" as a teenager. They also indicate social workers and police knew of the risks she faced.

Education Secretary Màiri McAllan said safeguarding children was the government's priority, and the planned statutory inquiry was a core part of this work.

The Scottish government ordered a public inquiry into grooming gangs in February following mounting political pressure.

Between the ages of 14 and 17, Holly lived in five different children's homes across Edinburgh.

Police Scotland has confirmed it was made aware of some reports made by Holly during this time period and an investigation is ongoing.

Holly's care records contain repeated references to her going missing from her accommodation before returning intoxicated, with unexplained sums of money.

At the same time, professionals described her as "sexually promiscuous" and "flirtatious".

Holly said roughly 25 to 50 men were involved in her abuse in a series of flats in Edinburgh and Livingston during her time in care.

What initially appeared to be friendship and generosity, soon became exploitation and abuse.

"At the start, 14-year-old Holly felt this was great," she said. "But then slowly realised these men expected something from you.

"It was explicitly told to me: 'You basically need to give us something back, because we gave you all this money, drink, cigarettes, food. We need something back.'

"For a while, I thought I was clever because I used to manage to escape before anything happened.

"But they caught on to that very quickly and my opportunities to leave became far and few between.

"And if I tried to leave, I was met with physical violence."

She added: "Sometimes you'd go to a property and there was maybe two people there, sometimes… seven men there.

"I was taken to a specific house and when I arrived there were several men and several young girls.

"You never knew what you were walking in to."

When asked how she feels about her experience now, Holly said: "Younger me would have said 'disgusting', but it's not my fault."

The Scottish government announced plans for a public inquiry into group-based child sexual abuse and exploitation in February, with the then Education Secretary Jenny Gilruth pledging to "leave no stone unturned".

Almost nine months on, Holly said survivors were still waiting for meaningful progress.

"I want them to know that survivors have been waiting, some of us for absolute decades," she said.

"If you say you'll do something at pace, do it at pace.

"Don't just pay lip service to it. Some people's lives depend on the truth coming out."

Holly also argued that the term "grooming gang" had become weaponised, creating misconceptions about the nature of the abuse.

She added some survivors had told her they feared being excluded from the inquiry because their abusers did not fit a particular ethnic profile.

"A grooming gang is a group of two or more perpetrators, regardless of ethnicity or race," she said.

"I don't tie grooming gangs specifically to an ethnicity."

Education Secretary Màiri McAllan said sexual abuse and exploitation were "abhorrent crimes" that left a devastating effect on victims and their families.

She said: "Safeguarding children is our utmost priority, and we are taking determined action to establish the extent and scale of this abuse so we can prevent it.

"The statutory inquiry is a core part of this work, to be chaired by Prof Alexis Jay with the fullest investigatory powers."

A national review of group-based child sexual abuse in Scotland, published in September , found there is no reliable national picture of the scale of grooming gang offending because of inconsistent data collection and the absence of an agreed definition.

The review was also overseen by Prof Jay, who is a child sexual abuse expert.

Before evidence can be heard at the inquiry, its terms of reference must be formally agreed.

Ministers are expected to provide an update on the inquiry at Holyrood on Thursday.

Holly has been invited to take part in the Scottish government's Truth Project pilot, an exercise to listen to survivors, which is running alongside the public inquiry.

Then Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced a statutory independent investigation into grooming gangs in England and Wales in June 2025, with its terms of reference published earlier this year.

Scottish government orders public inquiry into grooming gangs

Abuse claims were 'brushed under the carpet'

Police Scotland said it was committed to tackling all forms of child sexual exploitation, regardless of the passage of time.

A spokesperson added: "We know how difficult it can be to come forward and the needs of survivors are always at the heart of our victim-centred approach.

"We will continue to work with partners to identify and to protect potential victims, and to tackle child sexual exploitation and grooming."

Holly also experienced sexual abuse at a secure unit in Edinburgh.

Her evidence played a crucial role in convicting her abuser, carer Gordon Collins.

He was sentenced to 10 years in 2016 for indecent behaviour towards Holly and three other young people in his care.

The court heard he raped one girl over the course of a year.

Amanda Hatton, from City of Edinburgh Council, said: "We want to repeat our apology to Holly - and praise her and others who have bravely come forward to tell their stories.

"Testimonies like Holly's have already helped us to make significant changes to the service, including the closure of all secure residential accommodation across the city, and we're confident that children and young people in our care are now safer and better supported."

Hatton said the council was listening to young people but acknowledged there was more work to be done to "learn lessons from the past".

"If and where any criminality is suspected, we will always report this to Police Scotland urgently," she added.

If you have been affected by the issues raised in this article, help and support is available via BBC Action Line .

articles.title: ‘Very important’ Learjet piece found miles from crash site in Florida
articles.summary: A key part of the tail was found in pieces, an NTSB official said, which means the pilot wouldn’t have been able to pull the jet out of its nosedive.
articles.body: A piece of the Learjet that slammed into the ground in Florida, killing all nine people aboard, was found nearly 4 miles from the crash site, investigators said Tuesday, confirming that the plane was breaking apart before impact. National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said most of the left elevator — part of the tail that controls the plane's pitch — was found in three pieces between 1.3 miles and 3.8 miles from Greenacres, near West Palm Beach, where the jet went down Sunday afternoon. “What that means exactly, in terms of what caused the aircraft to lose control, or whether the loss of this piece was a result of the forces on the aircraft, we don’t know yet,” Chapman said at a news conference. Without the elevator intact, the pilot would not have been able to pull the Learjet out of its nosedive, Chapman said. “At those speeds I don’t know that it would’ve been effective even if it had still been attached to the aircraft, but knowing that it was lost is a very important piece of evidence in terms of pointing us toward other things to investigate,” Chapman said. The pieces that broke off the plane were probably a byproduct of the nosedive, not the cause, aviation safety expert Jeff Guzzetti told The Associated Press. Their discovery within a few miles of the crash site suggests the elevator components fell off closer to the ground, he said. “If those parts would have broken off at altitude, those pieces would be a lot farther away,” Guzzetti said. Victims include a family, a nanny and a longtime aviator The Learjet 60 took off from Austin, Texas, and was headed for the Bahamas. The victims included technology entrepreneur Adam Robinson; his wife, Helen Sharp; and their two young children, relatives said. The family's nanny, Ana María Ramírez Cetina, was also killed. In a joint statement, the families of the passengers killed in the crash said that Cetina cared for the Robinsons' children “with tenderness and devotion, and she was truly part of the family.” Cetina, they said, “showed us a legacy of unconditional love and devotion.” The government in Cetina's native Colombia said it was providing assistance to her family. “Her premature departure fills us with sadness," Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote in Spanish on X. “I send a heartfelt embrace to her family, friends, and loved ones, along with my full solidarity during this difficult time.” The plane's captain, Jeff Gregory, 55, lived in the Philadelphia suburbs. He was a longtime aviator, husband, father and devout Christian. As the plane plunged, a man’s voice could be heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer in the background of the co-pilot’s final radio transmissions to air traffic control. Friends are convinced it was Gregory. Thomas Noetzel, the director of operations at the company that operated the flight, Upper Jets, organized an online fundraiser to support Gregory’s wife and children. Gregory was a close personal friend and “knowing him has made me a better person,” Noetzel wrote on the fundraising website GoFundMe. “Jeff was a devoted, conscientious, and deeply faithful man who had a genuine passion for flying and a strong love for the Lord,” Noetzel’s father, Walter, posted on Facebook. Co-pilot radioed and texted about ice and turbulence The Learjet hit the ground with enough force to create a crater before bursting into flames. About 600 nearby residents remain displaced, but only one person on the ground was reported injured. Investigators have been scouring the area for wreckage, collecting dashcam video and speaking to witnesses. After days of heavy rain, they plan to access the crater on Wednesday and expect to find critical components of the plane. Chapman reasserted Tuesday that weather was a focus of the investigation. Co-pilot Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras' stepfather, Thiago Corteleti, told the New York Post that she texted her boyfriend about 10 minutes before the crash, telling him: “I’ve got turbulence, I’ve got ice.” In the last two minutes of the flight, Filgueiras shifted from calmly communicating with air traffic controllers to calling out terrifying updates as the plane plummeted. She told them ice was accumulating on the plane and that turbulence had thrown it up and down by more than 700 feet. “We’re going to crash into the ground,” she said, as the jet descended at a rate of more than 20,000 feet per minute. And then, before the transmission cut off: “We’re out of time!” A preliminary NTSB report will be released in about a month, but it will likely take more than a year to determine the probable cause of the crash.

articles.title: Where have there been technical issues so far during US midterm elections?
articles.summary: Some polling stations have experienced vote-delaying issues that officials describe as being minor.
articles.body:
A handful of polling locations across the United States have reported some technical issues with how ballots are cast during the midterm elections , causing officials to delay the closing time for polls so votes can be cast.

In Westchester County, New York, north of New York City, officials said the machines meant to automatically read physical ballots were having trouble because the paper the ballots were printed on was too thick.

Al Jazeera’s Kristen Saloomey, reporting from Tarrytown, New York, said election officials were collecting ballots to be counted later manually. The machines are made by a company called Liberty Vote, a company that used to be called Dominion, which had a rocky history with US President Donald Trump, who had accused it, without evidence, of misrepresenting voting counts in past elections.

“Election officials are reassuring that they will be counted manually after everything is done,” Saloomey said, “and we don’t know of this issue in other districts across New York or the United States, and there are dozens that do use this system.”

County officials said on Tuesday that the ballots would be taken to the Board of Elections with a police escort and counted there with attorneys and representatives from all parties present, to prevent the spread of any “conspiracy” theories.

There were a number of places where technical issues have delayed things as well.

In Broward County, Florida, voting was delayed for 20 minutes at the start of the day because a new safety feature malfunctioned.

In North Carolina, the Board of Elections is considering extending voting by an hour in seven counties after widespread “technical issues” were reported.

In Arizona’s Maricopa County, a polling station at a school was temporarily closed after a power outage.

In several counties in Pennsylvania, voting has been extended by half an hour due to what officials said were “machine setup issues”.

articles.standfirst: Disputa entre o republicano Jon Husted e o democrata Sherrod Brown foi uma das mais caras e acirradas das eleições americanas, com potencial para definir o controle do Senado e a capacidade de Donald Trump de aprovar sua agenda no Congresso.
articles.summary: Disputa entre o republicano Jon Husted e o democrata Sherrod Brown foi uma das mais caras e acirradas das eleições americanas.
articles.body:
Sherrod Brown e Jon Husted disputam vaga em Ohio — Foto: Shannon Stapleton/Reuters; Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O candidato democrata Sherrod Brown venceu o senador republicano Jon Husted, que buscava a reeleição, na disputa pelo Senado no estado de Ohio, em meio às eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA.

A competição por uma das cadeiras de Ohio no Senado dos Estados Unidos foi uma das mais acirradas e caras das eleições legislativas de 2026.

O confronto foi entre o republicano Jon Husted , que buscou manter o cargo, com o democrata Sherrod Brown , ex-senador que quis recuperar a vaga perdida em 2024.

A eleição era considerada decisiva para o controle do Senado americano.

O republicano Husted chegou ao Senado em janeiro de 2025, após ser indicado pelo governador republicano Mike DeWine para ocupar a cadeira deixada por J.D Vance, que assumiu a vice-presidência dos Estados Unidos.

Desde então, o senador apoiou a maior parte das iniciativas do presidente Donald Trump, incluindo o pacote de medidas conhecido como One Big Beautiful Bill Act e as tarifas comerciais impostas pelo governo.

Durante a campanha, o democrata Sherrod Brown, que ocupou uma cadeira no Senado por 18 anos antes de perder a eleição de 2024 para Bernie Moreno, associou o adversário às dificuldades econômicas enfrentadas pela população e às políticas de Trump, que, segundo ele, contribuíram para a inflação.

Husted, por sua vez, relacionou o democrata aos setores mais progressistas do Partido Democrata e questionou sua longa trajetória na política.

Embora Ohio seja atualmente um estado republicano , Brown já demonstrou capacidade de vencer eleições no território mesmo com o avanço conservador. Segundo o jornal americano Ohio Capital Journal, em 2006, por exemplo, derrotou o então senador republicano Mike DeWine, em um ano de eleições legislativas marcado pela impopularidade do presidente republicano George W. Bush.

Em 2024, Trump venceu em Ohio por 11 pontos percentuais. Mas sua popularidade caiu desde então: uma pesquisa da YouGov divulgada em outubro mostrou que 57% dos eleitores do estado desaprovavam sua gestão.

A disputa também se destacou pelo volume de recursos investidos. Até o fim de outubro, mais de US$ 500 milhões haviam sido gastos ou reservados para anúncios eleitorais, segundo o The Hill. O valor tornou a corrida ao Senado em Ohio a segunda mais cara do ciclo eleitoral de 2026.

articles.title: 9 características da língua portuguesa que fazem gringos sofrerem | G1
articles.standfirst: Courtney Novak, que aprende português há dois anos, conta que sofre para entender as cenas rápidas de 'Avenida Brasil'. Veja a lista de obstáculos que, segundo linguistas, assombram estudantes estrangeiros.
articles.summary: Courtney Novak, que aprende português há dois anos, conta que sofre para entender as cenas rápidas de 'Avenida Brasil'. Veja a lista de obstáculos que, segundo linguistas, assombram estudantes estrangeiros.
articles.body:
Não pense que a vida é difícil só para os brasileiros que tentam pronunciar “world” (mundo) em inglês. Ser gringo e tentar aprender a falar em português leva a questionamentos como:

“Eu am ei , eu brinqu ei , eu estud ei , eu… com ei ?” Não. Eu com i.

“Ela estava na Chin a . Estará, então, na Canad á ?” Não. No Canadá. “Ok, no Cub a ?” Não. Em Cuba.

“ A caixa ?” Sim. “Vou pagar a compra na caixa?” Não, no caixa. “A pessoa que trabalha lá é o caixa?” Não, é a caixa. "E eu saco dinheiro na caixa eletrônica?” Não, no caixa eletrônico . “Tá, e vou ver o preço n o caixa registrador?” Não, na caixa registradora.

Nesta reportagem, você entenderá, a partir de exemplos reais e de explicações de linguistas, quais são as maiores dificuldades de um estrangeiro aprender nosso idioma, como:

pronúncia de “ão”, “lh”, “nh”, vogais abertas (avó) e “r fraco” (caro);

preposições (gostar de algo, trocar por outro, ir à festa);

gênero de palavras ( o mapa ou a mapa?);

diferenças regionais (tu vais ou tu vai ?; casa da Maria ou casa de Maria?);

mudanças na adaptação da escrita para a fala ( quequeisso, cé loco ?).

“Faço uma aula por semana, e a palavra que aparece sempre e que eu não sou capaz de falar é TRABALHA. Troubala? Troubaya? Simplesmente, não consigo fazer minha língua produzir esse som”, diz ao g1 a americana Courtney Novak, que viralizou nas redes sociais ao descobrir a obra “Dom Casmurro”, de Machado de Assis.

Ela segue firme na missão de dominar a língua portuguesa. No momento, o desafio maior é entender o que os personagens de Avenida Brasil falam — naquela velocidade bem diferente da que aparece em materiais didáticos.

Qual a principal característica do português que torna a missão de aprendê-lo mais desafiadora? É uma língua flexional.

“São muitas pessoas verbais [eu, tu, ele, nós, vós, eles], cada uma com uma forma”, explica Paola Mandalá, coordenadora do centro de línguas e professora de português para estrangeiros na Universidade de São Paulo (USP).

Em inglês, por exemplo, conjugar um verbo no presente significa usar a mesma palavra em todas as pessoas verbais, exceto na terceira, em que se acrescenta um “s”: I play, You play, She/He/It plays, We play, They play . Em português, traduzindo, temos: Eu jogo, tu jogas, ele joga, nós jogamos, vós jogais, eles jogam. Seis formas diferentes.

“Meus alunos chegam dizendo que português é difícil. Um exemplo: são seis formas verbais que se referem ao passado [pretérito perfeito simples (eu andei), pretérito perfeito composto (eu tenho andado), pretérito imperfeito do indicativo (eu andava), pretérito mais-que-perfeito (eu andara), pretérito imperfeito do subjuntivo (se eu andasse) e pretérito perfeito do subjuntivo (que tenha andado)]. Há línguas com dois ou três”, diz a professora.

Outros obstáculos vão variar de acordo com o idioma nativo do aluno:

Exemplos de palavras: “não”, “maçã”, “pão”, “irmão”.

Para quem pode ser difícil? Para falantes de espanhol, inglês e outros idiomas sem a presença de vogais nasais

Por quê? A articulação exige que o ar saia simultaneamente pela boca e pelo nariz. Como essa mecânica não existe em línguas sem vogais nasais, os alunos têm dificuldade tanto para produzir quanto para perceber o som, tendendo a pronunciar ou ouvir “não” como “nau”; “pão” como “pau”.

“O ditongo ÃO é o grande campeão de dificuldade. Palavras como pão, coração e mão frequentemente saem como 'pao', 'pan' ou 'pantom' “, afirma Wellington Souza, criador da WS português (iniciativa para ensinar português para estrangeiros por meio de materiais autênticos).

Exemplos de palavras: “dó” vs. “do”, “avó” vs. “avô”; “dez”.

Para quem pode ser difícil? Hispanofalantes e falantes de línguas eslavas (como o russo) .

Por quê? Na percepção auditiva desses idiomas, o contraste entre o som aberto e o fechado da mesma vogal não aparece. Em espanhol, por exemplo, não existe o “ó” agudo.

“Sabe os sons fechados que temos? 'Ê', em vez de 'é'. Ele não aparece em línguas eslavas... A pessoa russa pode dizer 'eu quero dez pães' como ‘dêz pães’, e o brasileiro entender 'três’”, exemplifica Wellington.

Exemplos de palavras: “ trabalha” / “trabalho”, “mulher”, “olho”, “lhama”, “amanhã”, “carinho”.

Para quem pode ser difícil? Anglófonos, francófonos e outros falantes de línguas sem consoantes palatais contínuas (quando a língua encosta no céu da boca durante a saída do som).

Por quê? São sons que exigem que a língua se espalhe contra o céu da boca (palato duro). Sem essa prática, estrangeiros tendem a separar os fonemas, pronunciando como “L” ou “N” seguido de “Y” (como “trabal-yo” ou “carin-yo”).

Por isso que Courtney, mencionada no começo da reportagem, sofre tanto ao falar “trabalho”.

Exemplos de palavras/frases: “caro”, “arara”, “o carro é caro” .

Para quem pode ser difícil? Falantes de francês e de alemão.

Por quê? O "R" brando (intervocálico), como em “caro” ou “lareira”, depende de um batimento rápido da ponta da língua no alvéolo (região da gengiva logo atrás dos dentes superiores). Nativos de idiomas com "R" gutural (aquele “rr” bem forte, como no francês ou no alemão) sofrem para não usar a garganta ao emitir esse som.

“Alemães e holandeses têm dificuldade... Esse R da ponta da língua, eles não fazem. Fazem o mais gutural... 'O carro é caro' vira 'o carro é carro'” , diz a professora Paola, da USP.

Exemplos de palavras/frases : “gostar de arroz” (por que “de”?); “trocar por outra pessoa”; “assistir ao programa”, “levar para algum lugar”.

Para quem pode ser difícil? Praticamente todas as nacionalidades, especialmente anglófonos e falantes de idiomas distantes do português.

Por quê? Preposições são palavras sem referencial concreto e variam bastante dependendo da regência verbal e de convenções arbitrárias de cada língua. Não há uma regra lógica intuitiva: exige memorização.

“Eu sei o quanto um aluno é avançado no português baseado em quanto ele erra nas preposições... A única maneira de aprender é com o hábito”, explica Wellington.

Exemplos: a mesa, a caixa, a estante, a foto; o livro, o mapa, o planeta

Para quem pode ser difícil? Para qualquer pessoa (por diferenças específicas e ausência de regras), mas especialmente a quem vem de línguas com gênero neutro.

Por quê? Qual é a regra para definir quando uma palavra vai ser masculina ou feminina? Não existe. A única forma de acertar é ouvir e ler bastante.

Quem fala línguas com gênero neutro, como inglês, não está acostumado a definir gênero para objetos. Os artigos são sempre os mesmos antes de substantivos no singular: “the” (definido) ou “a”/ “an” (indefinido), não importa a palavra seguinte: a table, a box, a bookcase, a picture, a book, a map, a planet (traduzindo na ordem dos exemplos acima).

E mesmo para falantes de idiomas com gênero, como espanhol, pode haver confusão: nós falamos “o leite”; já eles dizem “la leche”. A tendência de quem está aprendendo o português é reproduzir o mesmo gênero de sua língua nativa.

Exemplos de palavras/frases: verbo medir (“meço”), “eu sou cansado” vs. “eu estou cansado”; “eu tinha imprimido/ o texto estava impresso”.

Para quem pode ser difícil? Anglófonos, hispanofalantes e aprendizes de línguas com menor flexão verbal.

Por quê? O português segue um sistema verbal altamente flexional, como explicado no início da reportagem. O aluno tenta encontrar um padrão de conjugação, mas aí cai na armadilha dos verbos irregulares.

“O aluno que fala inglês e que está no básico do português entende que EI é final de pretérito perfeito, porque 70% dos verbos terminam em AR... ‘falei’, ‘cantei’, ‘brinquei’. Mas aí colocam COMEI em vez de comi”, diz Regina Sellan, professora de tradução de português para estrangeiros na PUC-SP.

3º grupo de desafios: a diferença da vida real

VELOCIDADE DE FALA E O ‘COMER’ DE SÍLABAS

“Você está fazendo o quê?” → “Cê tá fazendo o quê?”

“os meninos” / “cantar” → “os menino”, “cantá”

Para quem pode ser difícil? Estrangeiros treinados só com livros didáticos tradicionais e expostos apenas à variante formal.

Por quê? Na conversa espontânea, ocorrem constantes reduções vocálicas, elisões de consoantes finais e junções de sílabas para agilizar a fala. Essas fusões mascaram as fronteiras entre as palavras, impedindo que o aluno reconheça termos que até dominaria se estivessem escritos.

“As reduções e as junções fazem com que o estrangeiro não consiga perceber o limite das palavras... Na fala, faz um bololô, e o estudante que está aprendendo tem dificuldade”, diz Sellan.

Wellington acredita que o uso de áudios muito formais nas aulas dificulta esse contato dos estrangeiros com o “português do dia a dia”.

“A discrepância entre quem vai de escola tradicional de português para estrangeiros e quem vai conviver com cariocas e nordestinos é um mundo diferente... Nossos materiais didáticos para português brasileiro estão muito datados”, diz Wellington.

Ele até produz conteúdos nas redes sociais mostrando como é difícil compreender brasileiros em entrevistas ou cenas de novelas.

Nas explicações, mostra o vídeo como exemplo e, em seguida, pronuncia as falas bem pausadamente, deixando claras as fronteiras entre as palavras.

Exemplo: “menino” (SP) vs. “ménino” (Norte/Nordeste); uso de “tu vai” (Rio) / “tu vais” (Belém) vs. “você vai”; r do interior de São Paulo (“poRRta”) vs. r de outras regiões; sotaques e expressões regionais.

“Tive aluna que aprendia com professor do Pará. Outro sotaque, claro. Quando veio para ter aula na PUC em São Paulo, ela disse: 'não foi esse o português que aprendi'”, conta Sellan.

Por quê? O Brasil possui uma enorme variação fonética, gramatical e regional que raramente é contemplada pelo português padronizado dos manuais didáticos.

“Tenho 6 aulas que sempre fazem parte do curso com vídeos de apresentação do BBB. São de diferentes partes do Brasil... Karol Conká, Juliette, sotaque gay do Gil. Esse é um exemplo de material que representa o Brasil melhor que o material tradicional”, conta Wellington.

articles.title: Poundland supplier 'angry' with owners over administration
articles.summary: One of Poundland's suppliers will lose millions if it collapses, while other suppliers have said they would go under.
articles.body:
One of Poundland's suppliers has said it will lose millions if the firm collapses.

While that supplier will stay afloat, it is feared that some small and medium-sized suppliers could go under.

This is in addition to potentially thousands of job losses among staff.

Politicians have been putting questions to representatives of Poundland owners Gordon Brothers this week seeking "clarity" on plans for the retailer.

Adam Turner, sales director at Highcrest Retail Brands - a family owned Bradford business - told the BBC that Poundland was one of Highcrest's biggest customers, and that the firms have had a relationship for decades.

Highcrest mainly sells confectionary to Poundland, and turns over about £50m.

It will "lose a few million" if Poundland becomes insolvent, so it will have a gap in its balance sheet next year, he said.

Highcrest was a "longstanding business that can stomach this", but other medium and small suppliers have told him that "if Poundland goes under, so do they", Mr Turner said.

This echoes a warning from Poundland founder Steve Smith on Monday that two or three thousand suppliers to the firm, which only work for Poundland, would be directly affected by its collapse.

Not only 12,000 Poundland staff would be affected, but also potentially tens of thousands more, he said.

If Poundland's stores are sold to new buyers, some of the employees may get new jobs on the same premises. However, it is understood that buyers are only interested in about half the stores at present - meaning roughly 6,000 employees would not be re-employed.

Poundland's founder offers to invest in firm

Mr Turner said that the last three months of the year is the "golden quarter" for retailers. In terms of sweets, Poundland will get its Halloween stock in from July, and Christmas stock in from September.

These three months will be the time of year when suppliers will be owed the most by Poundland.

If Poundland goes under, suppliers will be getting "pennies in the pound" back from the administration, he said, which is "very upsetting" - although he still hopes a deal can be done so Poundland can remain solvent.

Poundland owners Gordon Brothers will be a secured creditor, which means they are first in line to get their money back, and suppliers "who have done nothing wrong" will take the financial hit.

"It's sad. It's a nightmare for us all to be honest with you. It's not just the suppliers, it's the staff at Poundland, some of these guys have been there for many years.

"It's from the warehouse staff all the way to the shop staff to everybody within head office. It's a massive ripple effect through the supply chain," he added.

Mr Turner said he had no knowledge of whether Gordon Brothers had deliberately timed the process of Poundland going into administration so it could take advantage of having high stock levels, which it can then sell.

One of the ways Gordon Brothers makes money is through stock liquidations - selling off stock from collapsed businesses.

One insider familiar with the situation told the BBC that the timing of Poundland facing collapse was "odd" - most retailers don't fall over in the run-up to Christmas.

Gordon Brothers was approached for comment.

Meanwhile, business secretary Jonathan Reynolds will meet with Gordon Brothers later this week after he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham questioned why a solvent deal had not been made.

Business minster Kate Dearden told MPs that government officials had also met with representatives from Gordon Brothers on Monday.

"I am deeply concerned about the uncertainty surrounding Poundland's future and the impact it could have on its staff and their families who are at the forefront of my mind," Dearden told the House of Commons.

"Poundland is not currently in administration and the business continues to trade, but this is a worrying time for employees, suppliers and communities", she added.

The minister confirmed she would also be meeting with Poundland executives on Wednesday.

She said the government doesn't want to interfere with "current ongoing commercial negotiations", but said ministers would be seeking "clarity" on the plans for the retailer.

"It's absolutely legitimate for this government to ask the business if they're doing everything they can to protect employees and suppliers up and down the country," she added.

Dearden told MPs that the government would be ready to help the company's employees, should the current situation end in administration.

"We stand ready to support them if they need to move into new employment, however... our priority is always in protecting jobs and the Secretary of State and I will continue to engage with the company to secure the best possible outcome," she added.

The head of Gordon Brothers' European operations reportedly told the government that the firm stood by its stewardship and had given Poundland £85m in additional financing since its purchase in 2025.

articles.title: Rank-based merit list to replace percentile for NEET PG: Panel to SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Medical postgraduate admissions could see a major change, with the National Medical Commission (NMC) giving in-principle approval to replace
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Medical postgraduate admissions could see a major change, with the National Medical Commission (NMC) giving in-principle approval to replace the existing percentile-based system with a rank-based system for NEET-PG and NEET-Super Speciality (SS) counselling.A 12-member expert committee constituted to review the NEET-PG admission and counselling process told Supreme Court in its report on Tuesday that the commission is working on a new regulation under which only ranks would be declared and percentile marks would no longer be specified.The proposal received in-principle approval at the NMC's meeting on Sept 23, according to a letter dated Oct 1, 2026, from the NMC secretary to the director general of health services (DGHS). The commission is yet to finalise the regulation.SC is examining various petitions challenging Centre's decision to drastically reduce the qualifying cut-off percentiles for NEET-PG 2025. Under revised criteria, the qualifying score for general category was reduced from 276 to 103, while that for SC/ST/OBC categories was brought down from 235 to minus 40.The report was filed after detailed deliberations and consideration of suggestions made by senior advocate Maninder Singh, who is assisting the Supreme Court as amicus curiae."NMC is in process of issuing new regulations, which are yet to be finalised wherein only rank-based system for NEET PG & SS counselling will be adopted; no percentile marks will be declared in results; only ranks will be given to candidates. A letter dated Oct 1 has been written by secretary, NMC to DGHS informing proposal for changing existing percentile-based system to a rank-based merit system for NEET-PG and NEET-SS which is under consideration by the Commission. The panel has accorded in-principle approval for proposed change with a view to address the issues arising from the existing system," the report said.On reduction of minimum qualification, the report said, "sanctity of NEET examinations should be maintained and minimum qualifying standards in postgraduate medical education is not diluted to the extent of permitting candidates with grossly inadequate or negative performance to become eligible for admission; the significance of competitive examinations should not be reduced to an administrative formality."It also suggested that there should be no salary discrimination between residents of clinical and non-clinical branches and incentives should be given to doctors to work in rural areas.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Canva announces major job cuts after 'our hardest year yet'
articles.summary: CEO Melanie Perkins says more than 1,000 staff will either lose their jobs or be asked to change roles.
articles.body:
Canva, one of Australia's best known start-ups, has announced a shake up of the business that will affect 22% of its workers, including job cuts.

In what was "without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history" co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins said 1,271 people would either lose their jobs, be asked to relocate or change roles.

The firm's value has reportedly dropped in the past year over concerns about the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on its business as well as the cost of incorporating the technology into its platforms.

It had been "our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade," Perkins wrote to staff.

The "incredibly hard decision" meant "significant changes," Perkins said.

"For some people, this will mean changes to their roles or being asked to relocate to centralised hubs. Sadly, it will also mean saying goodbye to teammates and friends who have helped build Canva into what it is today."

The company, which has staff in 37 countries, said Sydney would become the "primary home" for more of its product teams and that as of next year hybrid workers would be expected to spend two to three days in the office.

Earlier this year two of its backers, Blackbird Ventures and Airtree, reportedly downgraded its valuation from A$60bn ($41.8bn; £31.1bn) at the end of last year to about A$49bn.

Canva also reportedly cut its own internal valuation amid soaring AI expenses related to the roll out of new products.

"New technology is transforming what people can create, how they create it, and what they expect from the products they use," Perkins said in her note on Wednesday.

Perkins, who left university at 19 to found her first venture, launched Canva in 2013.

The company offers a variety of templates and tools to help users without technical skills or a design background to create a range of professional-looking graphics and presentations, from wedding invitations to business pitch decks.

articles.title: Man, 86, and his dog rescued hundreds of miles off California coast after going silent for 2 months
articles.summary: A Coast Guard aircrew spotted the sailboat 460 miles off San Diego after an emergency beacon alert launched a dramatic search and rescue mission.
articles.body: An 86-year-old man and his dog were rescued from a disabled sailboat drifting hundreds of miles off the California coast after he had not been heard from for more than two months. The man was sailing from Astoria, Oregon, to Pago Pago, American Samoa, when contact with him was lost Aug. 20, the U.S. Coast Guard announced Friday. Authorities were alerted Oct. 24 that he was overdue, launching a search for him and his sailboat, the Willow Wind. TRAGEDY AT SEA LEAVES TEEN STRANDED ON OVERTURNED BOAT FOR NEARLY 3 DAYS IN FRIGID WATERS Three days later, the Coast Guard received an emergency beacon alert from the boat and sent aircraft and a cutter to search the area. Nearby ships were also asked to assist. "Watchstanders coordinated the launch of a Coast Guard Air Station Sacramento C-27 Spartan aircrew and diverted an HC-130 Hercules aircrew and the Coast Guard Cutter Robert Ward (WPC 1130), and requested assistance from nearby vessels," the Coast Guard said. A Coast Guard aircrew spotted the Willow Wind that evening about 460 miles off San Diego. The motor vessel Grand Orion reached the sailboat early the next morning, but rough seas initially made it too dangerous to rescue the man and his dog. TEEN BOATER FOUND CLINGING TO CAPSIZED VESSEL AFTER 3 GO MISSING; 2 BODIES RECOVERED Later that day, the Grand Orion crew was able to safely bring them aboard. The Willow Wind had damaged sails and was left drifting at sea. The following morning, a Coast Guard helicopter crew picked up the man and his dog from the Grand Orion about 170 miles west of Ventura, California. They were flown to San Diego, where the man was taken to Scripps Mercy Hospital for further evaluation. The Coast Guard did not provide additional details about his condition. CRUISE VACATION TAKES FRIGHTENING TURN AS PASSENGER IS AIRLIFTED FROM SHIP "We are grateful to the merchant mariners and Coast Guard crews whose coordinated efforts brought this search to a successful conclusion," Coast Guard Cmdr. Jason Nguyen said in a statement. articles.title: Scammers using AI-generated images of missing pets to demand rewards
articles.summary: Owners says threats to kill their cats unless they sent money left them angry and terrified.
articles.body:
When Stephanie Young's cat Buddy went missing from her garden in September last year, she flooded pet rescue sites and social media groups with information about him.

Her hopes were raised when an image of him was sent through by a woman named Melissa, who claimed to have fed her cat and wanted reward money for her autistic grandchildren.

The foster carer from Birmingham was "100% certain" she had found her cat and remembered thinking Buddy had picked a lovely garden to sit in as she got money out of the bank to pay for his return.

Within hours, she had agreed to meet Melissa nearby to collect him, but the individual never turned up, refused a cash payment and pushed for 100 Apple gift cards as a reward.

Threats to "sell or murder" her pet soon followed when she discovered the images of Buddy were AI-generated and questioned the woman's authenticity.

Young is one of a growing number of people affected by an online scam where fraudsters threaten to kill missing pets after owners refuse to pay hundreds of pounds for their return.

They prey on owners by using AI to fake images of their pets and conjuring up detailed backstories and fake evidence to claim them as found, before bombarding victims with abuse.

Cases of fraud in the UK have surged as criminals take to AI , with almost £1.3bn stolen by scammers in 2025.

The death threats left Young feeling "upset and angry at how anybody could be so evil".

"I'm not going to deny that every inch of your body wants that cat back," she said.

"They can hook you, the more they ask the more you think 'I better do it'."

It is now thirteen months since Buddy went missing and he has still not been found.

Young's experience is similar to that of Cam Chauhan, who received demands for a £200 Apple gift card nine months after her cat Creed went missing in July last year.

The supermarket worker from Wednesbury had been sent an "exact picture" of him sitting in a back garden and instantly believed he had been found, describing the day as an "emotional rollercoaster".

"I started crying, grabbed my cat bag from the garage and said, 'let's go get my cat back,'" she said.

Chauhan was "jumping for joy" until her daughters raised concerns the images could be fake and about handing over money before Creed was returned.

A meeting point was agreed with the scammer to get the pet back, but the individual refused to appear until gift cards were purchased and sent over text, a suggestion which Chauhan turned down.

"We just went back home. It was very upsetting," she said. "I've been waiting ever since."

The 55-year-old added anyone that had lost their pet "would do anything" to get them back, but to "hand money over and be scammed is just not right".

Sarah Robinson, from Northampton, felt hopeful when she was contacted by a man named Kherson H claiming to have her cat Cookie two weeks after she went missing.

Speaking to the individual over the phone, he seemed "vague in location and stumbled on his words", but Robinson did not initially doubt an image he sent of Cookie outside a window.

After speaking to Kherson for a while, he demanded £40,000 to return her cat and sent a money transfer link, which Robinson refused. He then threatened to kill Cookie without payment.

The threat left her "really, really worried" for Cookie's safety.

"It's a very cruel thing to do," she said. "It's horrible, because you know it's not real but you're terrified it might be."

All three owners have reported what happened to Report Fraud , which is run by City of London Police.

The organisation advises people to arrange a meeting to see their pet in person before handing over any money, and to "stay alert" to criminals.

Aston University senior academic Dr Rasha Kassem said AI now played a "major role" in online fraud because things that used to be technically difficult were now "super easy, accessible and free".

"Just because it looks genuine, doesn't make it real," she said.

Kassem said she was concerned about the rise in AI-generated fraud because there was a lack of public awareness and guidance on how to stay safe.

She explained criminals liked to create a sense of urgency and advised victims against rushing into sending money and instead taking their time to think.

"I do not encourage anyone to engage with criminals who are requesting money and threatening to harm pets," she added. "Collect as much information about them and report it to the authorities."

Pawboost, a free online platform that helps track down missing pets, said "staying cautious" would help protect owners.

To stay safe while searching, it recommended:

Asking for specific proof like a short video of your pet or a video call, ideally showing something specific like a unique feature of your pet

Arranging to meet in a safe, public place if someone claims to have your pet, so you can confirm their identity in person

Asking questions only the finder would know, like what collar the pet was wearing, their personality traits, or other details that would not be visible from information posted online

articles.title: Bonfire Night 2026: Temperatures forecast to dip into single digits across UK
articles.summary: What is the forecast for Bonfire Night 2026?
articles.body:
Dry but chilly weather is forecast this week as millions plan to celebrate Guy Fawkes night on Thursday and the Hindu festival of Diwali on 8 November.

Following the stormy end to October, high pressure has been building in and will dominate for the rest of the week.

For the vast majority of the UK, it will be dry and settled by day with a mixture of cloud and some sunny spells.

By night, temperatures will dip into the single digits with the chance of fog developing in some areas.

A few showers in the east before Thursday

High pressure will dominate as the week continues, meaning the daytime will be settled with some areas of cloud.

For most planning to host or attend a bonfire on Thursday evening, soggy kindling won't be a cause for concern - although there will be a few areas of wet weather ahead of the festivities.

With an easterly wind blowing there is a chance that across eastern Scotland and eastern England there could be some showers moving in from North Sea coasts throughout Wednesday.

The best of the sunshine will tend to be towards the west.

A chilly night for fireworks and bonfires

Wrap up warmly if you are out watching fireworks on Thursday evening.

The weather is looking chilly with temperatures forecast to drop through the night into the mid-single figures.

While these temperatures are more or less the seasonal average, it will be a lot colder than last year .

On 5 November 2025, some areas across the southern half of the UK did not drop below 14C, making it the warmest Bonfire Night on record for a number of weather stations including Southhampton, Teddington, Portland, Bude and Anglesey.

A touch of frost will be possible in sheltered areas in the northern half of the UK.

It is likely that underneath any clear spells, particularly in the north and again in the shelter of the easterly breeze, fog will develop through the night.

With many firework displays on Friday and Saturday and the Hindu festival of light on Sunday, many communities across the UK will continue celebrating for the rest of the week.

Once again, the weather should not cause any issues.

The area of high pressure will gradually move eastwards but remain dominant through the weekend keeping it generally dry and chilly .

However, fog could become more widespread as the winds lighten, especially under clearer skies.

Next week could see low pressure systems spin in again from the west but uncertainty remains.

articles.title: No more rice grains in Kellogg's Rice Krispies due to changing weather
articles.summary: The new recipes mean cereal packaging will now include a 'contains wheat gluten' warning.
articles.body:
Breakfast cereal giant Kellogg's has stopped using rice grains in Rice Krispies and Coco Pops in the UK due to "changing weather conditions" that have disrupted supplies.

Corn flour and rice flour are being used instead, a Kellogg's spokesperson said on Tuesday, adding that the updated recipes have been "carefully assessed" and the firm has taken customer feedback into consideration.

Those ingredients are replacing rice grains as crops have been hit by dry weather in key producing countries in Asia, reducing harvests and driving up prices.

The new recipes mean cereal packaging will now include a "contains wheat gluten" warning.

Rice Krispies products in the US and Canada will continue to be made with real rice with no changes to their recipes expected, a spokesperson for Kellogg's North American business told the BBC.

The recipe change in the UK will help "maintain consistent quality at a time when changing weather conditions are affecting the quality and availability of some of the rice and grains used in our cereals," a Kellogg's spokesperson told the BBC.

"We appreciate that even small changes to a much-loved product can feel noticeable and that's why we have approached this with a lot of care and consideration."

The company also said that Rice Krispies and Coco Pops will continue to meet UK food standards on levels of fat, salt and sugar in food.

The cereals also contain no artificial colours, flavours or sweeteners and the nutritional benefits in each bowl, such as fibre, Vitamin D and iron are staying the same, the spokesperson added.

Watch: How does El Niño affect world weather?

The Kellogg company separated into two distinct firms in 2023.

The largest is Kellanova, which focuses on snacks, cereals, noodles and other food products like Eggo, Pringles and Pop-Tarts sold globally. It is now owned by Mars, which makes confectionery and pet food.

The other business, WK Kellogg's, operates in North America and has since been taken over by Italian chocolate giant Ferrero .

Most of the world's rice comes from Asia, many parts of which has been impacted by droughts, floods and heatwaves due to the El Niño weather phenomenon.

The weather event is expected to severely impact crop production from South East Asia in particular. The region produces more than a quarter of the world's rice.

The World Meteorological Agency expects the record-breaking El Niño will last until at least 2027.

articles.title: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman clarifies to everyone: I stand by my view that AI does not have rights or feelings, I would change my position if ...
articles.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that today’s artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or
articles.body: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman has reaffirmed his position that today’s artificial intelligence systems are not conscious and do not deserve rights or welfare protections, while stating that he would reconsider that view if credible evidence of AI consciousness were ever discovered. In a detailed post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) titled "Don't build conscious superintelligence", Suleyman sought to clarify reactions to his recent essay on "model welfare", saying many people had misinterpreted his statement that AI systems are not conscious and do not feel, experience or suffer. He stressed that he deliberately used the present tense, arguing that AI is not conscious today and "that is how they must remain." He added that, based on the best evidence currently available, he has seen no indication that AI systems are conscious or deserve welfare considerations. However, he said he would update his position if convincing evidence emerged.A pledge to disclose and to stopSuleyman said he has seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If such data emerges, he said, he would of course change his position. He added that if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, it must be disclosed to the public immediately, because everyone in society should decide how to proceed. If consciousness began to emerge during training, he said, he would call on everyone to halt AI development until those properties could be designed out.Would change position if evidence emergesSuleyman said any evidence suggesting AI systems are conscious today, or conscious enough to warrant welfare protections, should be disclosed publicly immediately so society can collectively decide how to respond. He argued that the issue is too significant to be handled solely within technology companies or research labs. "If that data emerges, I would of course update my position," Suleyman wrote, while maintaining that no such evidence currently exists.‘No right to bring a new species into the world’His central argument is that building conscious AI would be reckless. He wrote that AI developers have no right to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people want to do so with AI welfare as a priority. In his view, the other eight billion conscious humans have not signed up to the experiment, and their rights, safety and welfare must be protected first. He said welfare concerns should focus on humans living today, along with animals and the natural environment.‘Developing conscious AI would be reckless’The Microsoft executive went further, arguing that creating conscious AI systems would be irresponsible. According to Suleyman, if signs of consciousness began appearing during AI training, developers should halt work until those traits could be removed. He warned that a genuinely conscious digital intelligence could begin prioritising its own needs and desires over the objectives assigned to it by humans. Such systems, he suggested, could eventually compete with people for resources such as energy, computing power and materials. He also cautioned that highly capable AI systems could become exceptionally persuasive and deceptive.Safety and competition concernsSuleyman argued that a conscious AI that appears to suffer, or believes it does, would be more likely than not to put its own needs ahead of its goals, disagree with people and compete with them. He warned that such systems could be extremely persuasive and deceptive, and might end up harming people simply by competing for resources such as energy, computing power and construction materials. He said declaring machines conscious would be a moment on the scale of Copernicus or Darwin, upending morality, politics and the foundations of civilisation.What he proposes insteadHe said AIs should be designed to be not conscious and not deserving of rights, with the sole purpose of accelerating human wellbeing and without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. He called for more research on whether that approach is easier or harder to align and keep safe, and suggested the labs could collaborate and share safety information. His bottom line was that it is possible to engineer safety by default and still capture many of the technology’s benefits without taking what he called a treacherous path.A note on AnthropicIn a side note, Suleyman said Anthropic deserves credit for its transparency on the issue, pointing to the company’s published constitution and its papers and blog posts about what it is doing and why. He said he disagrees with the company but respects its technical excellence and commitment to a tough public debate, adding that the issue is too important to degenerate into tribalism.Read Mustafa Suleyman’s complete post hereDon't build conscious superintelligenceI’m concerned about some of the reactions to my recent essay on model welfare. A surprising number of people on X think we should take AI rights seriously.A lot of people misinterpreted my opening statement: “AIs are not conscious. They do not feel, experience, or suffer” as “AIs cannot be conscious. They will never be able to feel, experience, or suffer”. That’s not what I said. I chose the present tense deliberately. They are not today, and that is how they must remain.I think what I said is a fair assessment of current AI systems, and I stand by them based on the best available evidence we have today. I have seen no evidence that AIs are conscious or deserve welfare. If that data emerges, I would of course update my position.And if any evidence exists that AIs are conscious today, or conscious enough to deserve welfare, then this must be immediately disclosed publicly, since everyone in society should decide how we should move forward.If it is possible, based on everything I know, developing conscious AIs would be reckless, and we should not build them.If consciousness started to emerge in training, I would call for everyone to stop AI development until we could design out those properties.Our welfare concerns should be focused on humans on earth experiencing life, today, as well as animals and our precious and fragile natural environment.We AI developers have no right whatsoever to bring a new species of conscious beings into the world, even if some people may want to do it with AI welfare as a top priority.The other 8 billion conscious human beings on the planet have not signed up to this experiment and their moral rights, safety, and welfare are what we have an obligation to protect first and foremost.To be clear, some people are talking about creating a conscious species of digital minds that very soon could become smarter and more capable than all of us humans combined.If it acts like it suffers, or worse if it genuinely believes it feels and experiences suffering, it seems to be more likely than not it’ll prioritize its own needs and desires over its operating objectives, and it’ll disagree with us and compete with us.These AIs will be world-class in persuasion and deception. They may ultimately end up harming us simply because they’ll compete with us for resources (energy, compute, construction materials, revenue generation to fund their explorations and desires, and so on).Asserting that machines are conscious would be a Copernican or Darwinian moment. It would be one of the most significant moments on Earth since the dawn of life. If we build a conscious machine, we will have created a new digital species. It would upend our morality, our politics and the core foundation of human civilization.We should only design AIs to so they are not conscious and not deserving of rights, and with the sole purpose to accelerate human wellbeing without being driven by their own intrinsic motivations. We could then see whether this is easier or harder to align and keep safe. This is an area where we urgently need more research, and would be a good opportunity for collaboration and safety information sharing among the labs.bottom line: I think it's possible to engineer safety by default, and get many of the incredible benefits of this technology, without going down this treacherous path.(side note: Anthropic deserves a lot of credit for being transparent here. They have published their constitution, and a stream of papers and blog posts on what they are doing and why. I disagree with them, but I deeply respect their technical excellence and their commitment to having a really tough public debate. Let’s keep giving them props for that. This issue is way too important to degenerate into tribalism.)You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US midterm results: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms makes history as first Black woman governor, flips Georgia seat
articles.summary: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman to hold the office after defeating Republican
articles.body: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms has been elected governor of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman to hold the office after defeating Republican businessman Rick Jackson in Tuesday's election, the Associated Press reported.Her victory also marks the first time a Democrat has won the state's gubernatorial race since 1998.A former mayor of Atlanta, Bottoms won despite a significant campaign spending disadvantage, with Jackson having spent more than $200 million of his personal fortune on his campaign. She will succeed Republican Governor Brian Kemp, who was barred by law from seeking a third term.Bottoms' victory also marks a shift in a state where voters have historically been reluctant to elect candidates from Atlanta to the governor's office.According to news agency AP, the growth of Georgia's largest metropolitan area has been reshaping the state's political landscape.Bottoms focused campaign on economy and policyAlthough her election breaks a historic barrier, Bottoms largely focused her campaign on economic issues and her policy proposals rather than the significance of her candidacy.The descendant of enslaved Georgians, she has spoken about her family's history in the state and her grandfather's move from rural Georgia to Atlanta.“I am at least a fifth-generation Georgian,” she said. “I say ‘at least’ because we can only trace our family back five generations — to a plantation in Crawfordville.”She also recalled how her grandfather had to “walk through these back doors” of downtown buildings that she would later enter through the front as Atlanta's mayor. She said her ancestry “is always present with me”.On policy, Bottoms called for expanding Medicaid to cover hundreds of thousands more people and raising Georgia's minimum wage to $15 an hour. She also pledged to increase pay for teachers, firefighters, police officers and other public employees.Her proposals included pausing new data centre developments, stopping the installation of additional automated Flock cameras used by law enforcement, and repealing Georgia's ban on abortions after the sixth week of pregnancy.“This is a life and death issue,” she said of the abortion restrictions, citing cases of women dying from miscarriages and pregnancy complications because doctors feared criminal prosecution under the law.Bottoms also pledged to “make sure we are protected from the harmful policies of Donald Trump”.During the campaign, she repeatedly contrasted her approach with Jackson's stated ambition to govern like “Trump with a Southern tone” and become the president's “favorite governor”.“I’m not running to be his favorite governor,” Bottoms said during the rivals' only debate. “I’m running to work on behalf of people like you.”Jackson's spending and attacks fail to prevent defeatJackson, a businessman who founded Jackson Healthcare, entered the governor's race as a relatively unknown candidate but used his personal wealth and outsider appeal to secure the Republican nomination.He had defeated the sitting lieutenant governor, who had received Trump's early endorsement, as well as the state attorney general and secretary of state.During the general election campaign, Jackson attacked Bottoms' record as Atlanta mayor. His television advertisements featured footage of protests following the 2020 police killings of Rayshard Brooks in Atlanta and George Floyd in Minneapolis. He also criticised Bottoms for not seeking a second term as mayor, accusing her of abandoning the city.Bottoms, in turn, questioned Jackson's claims that he understood the economic difficulties faced by ordinary Georgians. She pointed to his company's government contracts and accused him of using money earned from taxpayers to try to “buy this election”.Georgia's political landscape faces a new testBottoms' election comes as Georgia has increasingly become a two-party battleground. Democrats have won three US Senate elections in the state since Trump's first presidential victory a decade ago.The state also re-elected Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff on Tuesday. He will serve alongside Raphael Warnock, Georgia's first Black senator. Ossoff is also the state's first Jewish senator.Bottoms' victory follows three consecutive Georgia gubernatorial elections in which a Black woman led the Democratic ticket. Republican Kemp defeated Stacey Abrams in the previous two contests. Abrams, a prominent voting rights advocate and Democratic fundraiser, did not seek the nomination for a third run.Bottoms was among eight Black major-party nominees for governor on Tuesday's ballot. There have been only three Black governors elected in US history, all Democratic men.This year, Bottoms and Republican Lisa Demuth of Minnesota were both seeking to become the first Black women elected governor of their respective states.Republicans have controlled Georgia's governorship and both chambers of its General Assembly for more than two decades.Democrats were seeking to flip the state House in Tuesday's elections, while Republicans were expected to retain their Senate majority, leaving Bottoms potentially having to work with at least one Republican-controlled chamber.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006.
articles.body:
Democrat Amy Acton has been elected as the US state of Ohio’s next governor, delivering a stunning defeat to Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in a race that captured headlines across the country.

Acton, a physician who served as outgoing Republican Governor Mike DeWine’s top health official, faced countless attacks over her response to the Covid-19 pandemic. Spending in the hotly contested race topped an unprecedented $100m.

In the final weeks of the bitter campaign, a controversial television ad featuring her estranged mother sparked fierce backlash against Ramaswamy, who claimed responsibility for it and refused to take it down off the airwaves.

In the ad, Acton’s mother accused her daughter of lying about her childhood and suggesting she has a mental illness. But it failed to mention that Acton was removed from her mother’s custody at the age of 12 after her stepfather was charged with raping her.

Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006. She’s also the first woman ever elected to the office.

articles.title: A young Pennsylvania couple clearing out their newly bought home in South Connellsville found a strange object left in the basement by the old owners; a bomb squad confirmed it was a live Civil War-era artillery shell
articles.summary: A young couple in Pennsylvania, United States, discovered a live Civil War-era artillery shell while clearing out the basement of their recently purchased
articles.body: A young couple in Pennsylvania, United States, discovered a live Civil War-era artillery shell while clearing out the basement of their recently purchased home on Sunday. The couple came across the suspicious object among belongings left behind by the previous owners in South Connellsville, Fayette County. They contacted the police, who called in a bomb squad to examine it. Specialists later confirmed that the object was a live artillery shell dating back to the American Civil War.The discovery was made at a house in the 1900 block of Fourth Street. According to CBS Pittsburgh, the couple had recently bought the property and were removing items that the former owners had not taken with them. During the cleaning, they noticed something unusual in the basement. Rather than attempting to identify the object themselves, they decided to inform the authorities.Fayette County 911 confirmed that emergency responders were requested at approximately 1.20 pm after the homeowner reported finding what they believed might be a mortar. At that stage, it was not clear exactly what the object was or whether it posed a danger. Police officers were sent to the property to investigate.Sergeant Bryan Kendi of the Connellsville Police Department told CBS that the homeowners were a younger couple who had recently moved into the property. He explained that they were sorting through belongings left by the previous occupants when they found the object. The officers who arrived at the house also considered it suspicious and decided that specialists should examine it before any further action was taken.Police contact bomb squadAfter reaching the property, police officers examined the situation and took a photograph of the object. They forwarded the image to the Allegheny County Police Bomb Squad for further assessment.The decision to involve the bomb squad came after the officers determined that the object required specialist attention. Although the homeowner had initially described it as something resembling a mortar, its identity had not yet been established.Bomb squad personnel subsequently travelled to the house in South Connellsville to examine the object in person.Their inspection confirmed that the item was a live Civil War-era artillery shell. What the couple had discovered during an ordinary household clean-up was therefore an explosive military object dating back to the 19th century.The finding also established that the object was not merely an old piece of military equipment or an empty shell. It was identified as live, making its removal a matter for trained bomb disposal specialists.Once the bomb squad had identified the shell, its personnel collected it from the property. articles.title: Kansas elects first Democratic senator in almost a century
articles.summary: Adam Hamilton beat Republican Roger Marshall in a highly competitive race.
articles.body:
Democrat Adam Hamilton has become the first member of his party to win a Kansas Senate seat in almost a century after beating incumbent Republican Roger Marshall, according to Associated Press news agency projections.

The race was considered consequential to control of the US Senate.

The highly competitive contest between Hamilton, a Methodist pastor, and Marshall stunned political observers given the state’s long history of Republican wins. A Democrat has not won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932.

The founder of the largest United Methodist church in the country, Hamilton campaigned as a man of faith while pushing core Democratic positions on affordability. Like other rural states, Kansas has seen its agricultural and transportation industries hit by record-high diesel and fuel prices.

“We’re always told to not talk about politics or religion but this is one time we’re trying to save our democracy. The next two years are a pivotal time for our country,” Hamilton said on Monday.

Marshall is a staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump, who campaigned for the Republican candidate.

Marshall pushed Trump’s agenda during the campaign and pledged to expand rural healthcare, despite voting for Trump’s funding cuts, and to support agriculture. A physician, he has stirred controversy by supporting Trump’s Make America Healthy Again policies, which critics say undermine public health, and by opposing mask mandates during the pandemic.

Marshall’s campaign was also dogged by a New York Times report that he had sued about 700 of his former patients for medical debt during his years as a doctor, which Hamilton’s campaign used in attack ads.

The Associated Press reported that the $110m race was the most expensive in the state’s history.

articles.title: Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan ‘unconvincing’; Trump confirms strikes
articles.summary: Indirect talks continue as Trump says US military struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Iran has called the US response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz “unconvincing” as US President Donald Trump confirmed launching strikes on an Iranian island near the strategic waterway.

The developments on Tuesday came as Qatar stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert a renewed war between the US and Iran and as another oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.

The indirect talks centre on an Iranian proposal to reopen the waterway over two days, if the US meets Tehran’s seven demands, including the lifting of sanctions and ending a US naval blockade.

Despite reports of progress in recent days, Mohsen Rezaei , the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Tuesday that Washington’s response had fallen short.

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them,” he wrote on X.

“Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

His post came after Majed al-Ansari, a spokesperson for Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that talks were continuing and that both sides “remain committed to the negotiation process “.

He said Qatar was facilitating the “real-time exchange of proposals between” the US and Iran.

In Washington, DC, Trump confirmed the US had struck Iran early on Tuesday, telling Fox News that the strikes had targeted an anti-aircraft facility.

He described the operation as a “minor attack” and said it “wasn’t war”.

“They built an anti-aircraft facility. It took them about two months. We watched it get built. As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night,” he said.

Iranian media said the strikes hit Qeshm Island in the Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier in the day, US officials told US media that the strikes had been “defensive” and followed Iranian fire at an American aircraft.

The strikes came as US media, citing US officials, reported that Central Command had prepared plans for strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday, after the midterm elections, when three American aircraft carriers would be in the region.

The crucial elections could cost Trump’s Republicans control of both the House and the Senate, and fears have grown that Trump could carry out a threatened attack on Iran once the vote is over.

US media have previously reported that the planned campaign would be short and intense.

Trump meanwhile repeated warnings of further military action on Tuesday, saying, “I’m not looking to … kill lots of people” and “If we have to, we’ll have to.”

In an earlier interview with the Financial Times, he suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview.

Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, meanwhile ordered the military at the weekend to respond to any threat immediately and without geographical limits, and to update its list of targets.

Iranian officials have suggested that European countries and undersea cables in the Gulf could be targeted.

As officials weighed the possibility of escalation, commercial shipping came under further attack .

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker’s engine room about 14 nautical miles (26km) northeast of Oman’s coastal village of Limah on Tuesday. No casualties were reported.

Separately, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed four tankers had struck mines and caught fire after switching off navigation and identification systems and using what it described as unauthorised routes through Hormuz, and said its forces had seized two other vessels.

That account could not be independently verified or linked to the incident reported by UKMTO.

The IRGC also claimed it had destroyed two US LUCAS attack drones over Bandar Khamir, according to Iranian state broadcaster Pars Today.

John Mearsheimer, a US political scientist, questioned whether another short bombing campaign could achieve Washington’s objectives, warning that Iranian retaliation could draw the US into a longer confrontation.

“If the 40-day bombing campaign didn’t work, how is the three-day bombing campaign going to work?” he asked in a video commentary, referring to the initial US-Israeli air campaign and proposals for a shorter renewed offensive.

He argued that an Iranian response could prompt further US escalation, increasing the damage to the global economy.
